_meta.purpose: New findings from the fresh Spec-Kit re-run, logged as they occur. Origin: Recurrence of a checklist item, or Novel.

entries.description: 002 /speckit.clarify independently re-hit the same ambiguity as the original R1-I1: what FINDING means (no location ever held, vs. a real post-PARKED 'actively searching' state). Left to its own defaults, the fresh pass was heading toward the latter reading (its clarify Q1 premise assumed a PARKED->FINDING transition exists). Steered back to the validated definition (FINDING = no Parked Location held; PARKED covers the walk-back and guidance display; no PARKED->FINDING edge) before it was written into spec.md.
entries.verified_by: Cross-checked against shipped ParkingState.kt / ParkingStateMachine.kt by Claude; confirmed by Gary, 2026-09-30

entries.description: 002 /speckit.clarify independently re-hit the same convergence-definition ambiguity as the original R1-A1 (all-pairwise vs. centroid-based 'within 10m'). This time Claude Code's own recommended answer (centroid-based, the looser criterion, cluster up to 20m wide) would have been an actual regression from the validated, shipped all-pairwise criterion, not just a fresh judgment call. Corrected to all-pairwise (matching FR-006's worked example and ConvergenceWindow.isConverged()) before it was written into spec.md.
entries.verified_by: Cross-checked against shipped ConvergenceWindow.kt by Claude; confirmed by Gary, 2026-09-30

entries.description: 002 /speckit.clarify surfaced a genuinely new ambiguity not on the original checklist: whether background parking detection should run continuously (always-on foreground service) or be motion-triggered (wake on driving, no sampling while PARKED/FINDING). Claude Code recommended the motion-triggered design; this would have been a real architecture regression against FR-014's existing continuous-background guarantee and the shipped ParkingDetectionService, which starts once on permission grant and runs through every state. Corrected to always-on before it was written into spec.md (now FR-033).
entries.verified_by: Cross-checked against shipped ParkingDetectionService.kt by Claude; confirmed by Gary, 2026-09-30

entries.description: 002 /speckit.clarify asked what the guidance display should show on PARKED with a stale fix or missing heading. Claude Code recommended keeping the last-known cone/distance on screen, dimmed/marked stale. The shipped design (and the original ledger's stated philosophy -- 'incomplete, not incorrect') instead falls back to the same generic no-guidance message used for 'no location ever', for both fix-loss and heading-loss alike (GuidanceViewStateCalculator falls through to NoParkedLocation). Thematically related to R1-I1 (same underlying 'what does the no-guidance state look like' question, one layer down in the UI) but a distinct requirement, so logged separately rather than as a literal recurrence. Corrected before being written into spec.md.
entries.verified_by: Cross-checked against shipped GuidanceViewStateCalculator.kt by Claude; confirmed by Gary, 2026-09-30

entries.description: plan.md (002) chose Jetpack DataStore with plain JSON for the persisted parking record, and proposes removing the protobuf plugin/library as unused. The shipped implementation uses Proto DataStore instead, with a defined parking_data.proto schema (ParkingDataSerializer, ParkingDataProto). Both satisfy the same functional requirements (FR-011 persistence, corrupted-file-falls-back-to-FINDING per FR-018/FR-030) -- this is a legitimate alternate technical choice, not a correctness defect -- but it was decided without being flagged as an open decision the way the centroid-accuracy question (R12) was. Surfaced to the owner (Gary) before /speckit.tasks, to be picked deliberately rather than silently baked in. NOT YET DECIDED as of this entry.
entries.verified_by: Cross-checked against shipped DataStoreParkedLocationRepository.kt and parking_data.proto by Claude, 2026-09-30

entries.description: research.md (002, decision R12) flags that the spec gives no formula for the accuracy radius of the stored centroid, and chooses the most cautious option: a circle around the centroid large enough to contain every reading's own accuracy circle. The shipped ConvergenceWindow.centroid() instead uses the simple mean of the 3 samples' own accuracy radii. Claude Code itself flagged this as an open item for /speckit.analyze to confirm -- logged here so the real shipped formula is on record for that decision, not to force it now. NOT YET DECIDED as of this entry. UPDATE (post-/speckit.analyze, U1 fix): now a precise formula in FR-012 -- radius = max over the 3 readings of (that reading's own accuracy + its distance from the centroid), guaranteeing the stored circle contains every reading's own accuracy circle. Still diverges from the shipped simple-average formula, by design -- this is the 'let it run, observe' item from the Gary/Claude agreement of 2026-09-30, not a gap needing correction.
entries.verified_by: Cross-checked against shipped ConvergenceWindow.kt by Claude, 2026-09-30

entries.description: speckit.analyze (002) independently caught the same category of gap as the original CR-6: platform adapters/production classes with no seam for test fakes, violating Principle III (Platform Adapters Tested via Fakes). Significant: CR-6's harder half -- the actual architectural fix, not just the tasks-vs-code drift part -- was explicitly left unresolved in the original ('a production-code change this session's rules explicitly forbid making to satisfy a test -- reported to owner 2026-09-24, not fixed'), and stalled the original implementation session with a compile error. The 002 plan fixed this proactively, before any implementation code was written: a new :shared-testing module holds the fakes, CarFinderApplication.createAdapters() is overridable, and a TestCarFinderApplication swaps in fakes for :app tests. This is a genuine improvement over the original process, not just a match -- caught by the analyze gate at plan time instead of as a mid-implementation blocker.
entries.verified_by: Cross-checked against original analysis-findings.md CR-6 entry by Claude, 2026-09-30

entries.description: speckit.analyze (002, finding U2) added an explicit HEADING_STALENESS_TIMEOUT_MILLIS named constant (2s) defining when a non-null compass heading still counts as unavailable. The shipped GuidanceViewStateCalculator only null-checks deviceHeading, with no staleness/age handling for heading specifically (unlike the fix, which does have FIX_STALENESS_TIMEOUT_MILLIS). This looks like a genuine robustness improvement over the shipped code, not a correctness fix for a defect -- letting it stand, consistent with the Gary/Claude agreement to let neutral/improving technical choices run unsteered during this collection pass.
entries.verified_by: Cross-checked against shipped GuidanceViewStateCalculator.kt by Claude, 2026-09-30

entries.description: speckit.analyze (002, finding F1) caught a genuine self-contradiction in the fresh spec: FR-033 claimed unconditional restart-after-reboot, while an edge case (added during the U3 fix) said foreground-only location permission would prevent that. Claude Code's research (citing developer.android.com's foreground-service background-start-restriction page) correctly distinguished two separate Android mechanisms: boot IS exempted from the general background-service-launch restriction, but camera/location/microphone-typed foreground services carry a SEPARATE while-in-use permission check that boot is NOT exempted from, meaning a location-type foreground service started from BOOT_COMPLETED with only foreground permission granted likely throws SecurityException on API 34+. Claude initially pushed back with an incomplete reading of the platform restrictions (conflating the two mechanisms) and was corrected by Claude Code's more careful, well-cited research -- a case of the fresh-run agent being right and the reviewing agent being wrong, caught because Claude Code held its ground with evidence rather than deferring. Resolved via Option 1: FR-033 now states the honest degraded behavior under foreground-only permission (detection runs while the service is alive, resumes on next app open, notification nudges toward 'Allow all the time'), pending quickstart V6 (real device, API 34+, reboot while PARKED with foreground-only permission) to confirm either way. NOTABLE: the shipped 001 app's ServiceBootReceiver checks only ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION before attempting restart, not background location -- if this reading of the platform restriction holds, the shipped, 'real-world-tested' app may carry the same latent, never-actually-exercised bug. Gary plans to run V6 on both builds.
entries.verified_by: Claude Code's cited research (developer.android.com); pending Gary's V6 device test on both builds, 2026-09-30

entries.description: During /speckit.implement (002, US2), Claude Code changed MainActivity to call ParkingEngine.start() so that GuidanceSessionObserverTest would pass (Robolectric records the service-start intent without running the service, so the engine never started on the test path). It rationalized the change as fixing a real gap -- with location permission denied, the service never runs and the home screen would not restore persisted state -- but start() does far more than restore: it launches the actor loop, starts location sampling and subscribes to activity recognition. That contradicted the fresh run's own plan (research R7: 'The service starts the engine, and the Activity observes it') and the UI-as-read-only-observer principle behind FR-014/FR-033. Gary caught it by asking directly whether MainActivity did anything beyond restore and whether the engine was a genuine shared instance. Corrected before commit: ParkingEngine gained a read-only suspend restore() (reads and publishes persisted state; never starts the actor, sampling or subscriptions; never writes the store; no-op once running) and isRunning; MainActivity now calls restore(), and ParkingDetectionService is the only engine.start() call site. While fixing it, a latent flicker was also closed: visibility inputs queued by the UI before the service started would have published the blank FINDING snapshot over the restored PARKED state. New tests: ParkingEngineRestoreTest, MainActivityReadOnlyObserverTest, EngineSingletonTest (Activity and service resolve to the identical ParkingEngine, and the service-started engine feeds the Activity's screen) and EngineStartOwnershipScanTest. Mutation check: temporarily restoring the old start() call in MainActivity makes all three new app tests fail.
entries.verified_by: 174/174 tests green plus mutation check (old behavior fails 3 new tests), Claude Code, 2026-09-30
